model_name: Model 5 - Volatility/Risk (EWMA vs naive rolling window)
notes: Different ablation shape than Models 1-4: tests whether EWMA volatility clustering-aware weighting beats a naive flat rolling window at predicting forward realized volatility, not return direction. h=1 excluded (undefined).
decision: ACCEPTED - the first model to clearly clear the bar. EWMA beats naive rolling-window volatility forecasting on RMSE at 100% of instrument-horizons (45/45), with meaningfully stronger correlation to actual forward volatility (mean 0.300 vs 0.284, and individual instruments up to 0.63 - far higher than any correlation seen in the return-prediction models). Consistent with well-established literature: volatility is far more persistent/forecastable than returns. HG_F shows negative correlation for both estimators (possible genuinely less-persistent copper volatility) but EWMA still wins there too. This becomes the production volatility estimate feeding downstream position sizing, EV-after-risk, and NO-TRADE gating.
influenced_later_decisions: EWMA(lambda=0.94) adopted as the volatility model. Next: ranking engine + NO-TRADE filter, per the direction decision after four rejected return-prediction models.

decision: Mixed, instrument-specific - NOT a blanket accept/reject. model_name: Model 7 - Equity Momentum (12-1 month; vs Model 1)
notes: Asset-class-specific model - equities only. Uses an expanding window for momentum-sign conditioning, not a fixed trailing lookback - a fixed 250-day window was tested and found to be a silent no-op (momentum barely changes sign within 250 days), caught before real-data testing. Multi-seed testing (n=25+15) confirmed no systematic fabricated edge on pure noise.
decision: ACCEPTED - the strongest, most consistent equity finding of the whole project. 91.7% RMSE win rate (11/12 combinations), with the improvement uniform across ALL THREE available stocks (AAPL 4/4, MSFT 4/4, NVDA 3/4), not concentrated in one or two names the way Model 3s equity result was (which showed MSFT/NVDA up but AAPL down). Consistent with 12-1 month momentum being one of the most replicated anomalies in finance (Jegadeesh and Titman 1993 and decades of follow-up). Multi-seed no-edge testing (n=25+15, ~44-73% range, averaging near chance) confirms 91.7% is well above what noise alone would produce. Recommend: change the STOCK asset-class default from Model 1 to Model 7, not just a narrow ticker override - this is broader, more uniform evidence than the CL_F case. [MULTIPLE-TESTING DIAGNOSTIC ADDENDUM, added after experiment #14]: scoped Bonferroni correction (accounting for the 2 other models - Model 1, Model 3 - actually tried on stocks) gives adjusted p=0.076 - BORDERLINE, not a clean accept. The 91.7% headline win rate overstates confidence once multiple-testing is properly accounted for. Downgraded from ACCEPTED to PROVISIONAL - kept as the stock asset-class default since it remains the best available evidence for this class, but should be treated as unconfirmed pending more out-of-sample data (e.g. more equities added to the universe, or more time elapsed).
influenced_later_decisions: Stock asset-class default changed from Model 1 to Model 7 in the ranking engine.
